name: daughter of the King of the South
overview: The daughter of the King of the South is a female figure identified specifically as the daughter of the king of Egypt, as noted in Daniel 11:6. Beyond this unique attribute, there is no additional tribal or personal information recorded about her in Scripture.
namesAndTitles: Her designation, 'daughter of the King of the South,' literally means 'daughter [of the] prince [of] the south,' indicating her royal lineage. This title is descriptive rather than a personal name and is not given by God, as referenced in Daniel 11:6.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies her as the daughter of the King of the South, who is the king of Egypt. No other family relationships are recorded for her beyond this connection.
scriptureSignificance: This figure represents a key royal connection in the prophetic vision of Daniel, symbolizing political alliances or interactions involving the king of Egypt. Her mention underscores the geopolitical dynamics between the northern and southern kingdoms described in Daniel 11:6, highlighting God's sovereign orchestration of earthly kingdoms and their relationships.
